606Spinal facilitation

What is spinal facilitation?

AnswerPANs release substance P in the dorsal horn → glutamate channels open → Ca2+ influx → more dynorphin → sensitized dorsal horn cells. Less input triggers a response (hyperalgesia, allodynia), increasing sympathetic and alpha motor outflow and producing TART changes.

Ans: Ongoing PAN input → dorsal horn sensitized → low threshold → ↑ SNS + motor output

Why: Spinal facilitation is a lowered firing threshold of a spinal segment after ongoing afferent input. The output is out of proportion to the input: more lateral horn (sympathetic) and ventral horn (alpha motor) outflow.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Results: hyperalgesia (noxious feels worse), allodynia (non-noxious feels painful), increased muscle tone and restricted motion, and sympathetic vasomotor and sudomotor changes, i.e., TART. The hypertonic muscle then adds more nociceptive input, keeping the cycle going; OMT aims to break that somatic part.

607asked 2×Acute vs chronic findings

What changes do you expect to see in an acute viscerosomatic reflex?

Ans: Acute VSR → inflammatory mediators → fluid leaks into subcutaneous tissue (boggy)

Why: In an acute reflex, inflammatory mediators cause subcutaneous fluid extravasation, which is why the tissue feels warm and boggy.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Each distractor is backwards: sympathetic activity reduces blood flow to the viscera, muscle tone increases (alpha and gamma outflow), and sweating increases. Also expect increased skin drag and tissue texture changes.

613Sympathetic levels

A 25-year-old woman comes to your office complaining of feeling down after her boyfriend broke up with her. On examination, her left paraspinal muscles are warm and erythematous at the levels of T1-T6. These palpatory findings indicate further investigation into which organ system?

Ans: T1-T6 = heart and lungs → left-sided → heart

Why: T1-T6 supplies the heart and lungs, and the heart tends to show left-sided findings.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Lungs share T1-T6 but are not specifically left-sided. Appendix is T10-T11 right; kidneys T10-T11; liver T5-T9 right; colon T10-L2; bladder T12-L2.

616Sympathetic levels

A patient presents with back pain that improves with manipulation only briefly, then returns the next day. On forward bending you find a rib hump on the right that begins at the spinous process of T3 and ends at the spinous process of T6. The TPs in that area are all rotated to the right and do not change in flexion or extension. You suspect a visceral origin. What is highest on your differential?

Ans: Recurring SD at T3-T6 → T1-T6 = heart/lungs → pneumonia

Why: Somatic dysfunction that keeps returning after OMT suggests a visceral source. T3-T6 sits in the T1-T6 heart and lung range, so pneumonia fits.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Hepatitis and gallbladder disease are T5-T9 right. Gastritis is T5-T9 left. The upper ureters are T10-T11. The IA5 version of this vignette puts the hump at T10-T12, which points to the upper ureters instead.

617asked 3×2026Sympathetic levels

A 15-year-old male presents to your office with an acute asthmatic exacerbation. Structural examination will most likely reveal tissue texture changes at

Ans: Asthma → lungs → T1-T6 → T2-T6

Why: The lungs' sympathetic level is T1-T6 in the course (T2-T7 in the textbook), so T2-T6 fits.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

C2-C7 has no sympathetic outflow (cervical ganglia get fibers from T1-T4). T5-T10 centers on the upper GI organs. T9-T11 is small bowel, kidney, and gonads. T12-L2 is the lower colon and pelvis.

Why: The gallbladder is upper abdominal viscera (T5-T9, celiac ganglion) and sits on the right. The lecture's own example: gallbladder inflammation causes acute changes at T7-8 on the right.

Explanation

A and C (T1-T4) are head, neck, heart, and lungs. D (T10-T12 right) is appendix, cecum, ascending colon, kidney. E points to vagal (parasympathetic) reflexes, not the expected sympathetic finding. The 2023 TA version offered 'T6-8 on the right' as the answer; same idea.

Why: The gallbladder belongs to the T5-T9 upper abdominal group, on the right with the liver, duodenum, and head of pancreas.

Why: The gallbladder maps to the T5-T9 upper abdominal group; T6-T9 is the only option inside that range.

Explanation & sources

622asked 3×2026Sympathetic levels

A 42-year-old obese female presents with right upper quadrant pain that radiates to the tip of the right scapula. Examination reveals severe pain while the patient inhales with your fingers beneath the right subcostal margin. At which vertebral levels would you expect to find somatic changes?

Ans: Positive Murphy sign → cholecystitis → T5-T9 → T6-T9

Why: This is a positive Murphy sign, so think cholecystitis. The gallbladder's reflex is T5-T9 (greater splanchnic nerve, celiac ganglion).

Explanation & sources

Explanation

T1-T4 is head and neck. T9-T11 is small bowel and kidney. T11-L2 is the lower GI and pelvis. L1-L4 extends below sympathetic outflow, which ends at L2.

623Sympathetic levels

A 41-year-old man presents to the ER with severe abdominal pain after eating 70 hot dogs in 10 minutes. He appears pale, cool, and diaphoretic with right paraspinal tenderness and bogginess at T5-T9. Based on your palpatory findings, what do you suspect?

Why: Right T5-T9 is the liver, gallbladder, duodenum, and head of pancreas. Acute bogginess fits acute cholecystitis.

Explanation

B (stomach) is T5-T9 but on the left. C (appendicitis) is T10-T11 right. A (kidney) is T10-T11. D and F are upper thoracic (T1-T6). G (prostate) is T12-L2.

624Sympathetic levels

625asked 2×Sympathetic levels

A patient's back pain improves with OMM briefly but returns the next day. On forward bending there is a rib hump on the left from the SP of T5 to the SP of T9. The TPs are all rotated left and do not change in flexion or extension. You suspect a visceral origin. What is highest in your differential?

Ans: Left T5-T9 → stomach, spleen, tail of pancreas → GERD

Why: Left T5-T9 is the stomach, spleen, and tail of the pancreas, so an acid or stomach problem like GERD fits best.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Prostate is T12-L2. Pneumonia is T1-T6. A UTI involving the upper ureters is T10-T11, lower ureter and bladder T12-L2. The recurring dysfunction after OMT is the clue to look for a visceral cause.

626asked 3×2026Sympathetic levels

A middle-aged male alcoholic presents with vague abdominal pain. Physical examination reveals scleral icterus, abdominal distension, and caput medusae. Sympathetic innervation to the pathologic organ passes through the

Ans: Jaundice + ascites + caput medusae → liver → T5-T9 → celiac ganglion

Why: The signs point to liver disease (alcoholic hepatitis or cirrhosis). The liver is T5-T9, via the greater splanchnic nerve to the celiac ganglion.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

E (superior mesenteric) is T10-T11 midgut. B (inferior mesenteric) is T12-L2 hindgut and pelvis. C (otic) is a parasympathetic head ganglion for the parotid. D is not a standard sympathetic ganglion.

627asked 3×2026Sympathetic levels

A middle-aged male presents with epigastric discomfort and heartburn. Structural examination will most likely find tissue texture abnormalities at which of the following?

Ans: Heartburn → vagus (C2 L) + esophagus (T3 R) + stomach (T5 L) → B

Why: The textbook pattern for gastritis or heartburn is C2 left (vagus), T3 right (esophagus), and T5 left (stomach).

Explanation & sources

Explanation

The other options describe right-sided, block, or lower patterns that do not match the esophagus and stomach. This specific pattern comes from the textbook chapter; the 2026 slides only teach the broader rule that the stomach is T5-T9 left and vagal viscera relate to OA-C2.

You palpate the left lower quadrant of your patient's abdomen and they feel pain in the right lower quadrant, indicating appendicitis. Where would you expect tissue texture changes?

Why: The appendix, cecum, and ascending colon map to T10-T11 on the right (superior mesenteric ganglion).

629asked 3×2026Sympathetic levels

A viscerosomatic reflex resulting from a right colon cancer would be associated with somatic changes at which spinal segment?

Why: The right (ascending) colon is midgut, mapped to T10-T11 on the right via the lesser splanchnic nerve and superior mesenteric ganglion.

Explanation

632asked 5×2026Sympathetic levels

A patient presents with acute diverticulitis in the sigmoid colon. Where would you expect to palpate tissue texture changes along the spine?

Ans: Sigmoid colon = hindgut → inferior mesenteric → T12-L2

Why: The descending and sigmoid colon map to T12-L2 (inferior mesenteric ganglion), along with the lower ureter and pelvic organs.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

OA-C2 is vagal, which stops before the descending colon. T1-T5 is head, neck, heart, lungs. T5-T9 is upper abdominal viscera. T10-T12 is small bowel, kidney, gonads, and the right colon. Asymptomatic diverticulosis without inflammation usually gives no significant VSR findings.

633Sympathetic levels

A 25-year-old male comes to the ER with abdominal pain, nausea, fever, and constipation. He is diagnosed with diverticular disease of the sigmoid colon. His muscles are warm and erythematous at the level of T12-L2. Which ganglion is most likely affected?

Ans: Sigmoid colon, T12-L2 → inferior mesenteric ganglion

Why: T12-L2 organs (descending and sigmoid colon, lower ureter, pelvic organs) are served by the inferior mesenteric ganglion.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

C (celiac) is T5-T9. D (superior mesenteric) is T10-T11. A (cervical ganglia) supply the head, neck, and heart from T1-T4. The source called this diverticulosis, but fever and warm, red tissue imply inflammation (diverticulitis); plain diverticulosis usually gives no significant VSR.

Why: This is likely benign prostatic hyperplasia. The prostate and other pelvic organs map to T12-L2, so L1 is the answer.

Explanation

T5 and T8 are upper GI. T11 is kidney, upper ureter, and gonads. S2 is parasympathetic (pelvic splanchnics), not the sympathetic viscerosomatic level the key is looking for.

635asked 3×2026Sympathetic levels

A 25-year-old female presents to your office with dysmenorrhea. Viscerosomatic reflex changes associated with uterine dysfunction may be at which spinal level?

Ans: Uterus = pelvic organ → T12-L2 → T12

Why: The uterus is a pelvic organ, sympathetic level T12-L2 in the course (T10-L2 in the textbook). T12 is the only option in range.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

AA relates to vagal reflexes, which do not reach the uterus. C7 has no sympathetic outflow. L4 is below L2. Uterine parasympathetics come from S2-S4, not S1.

636asked 3×2026Parasympathetic levels

A newborn receives a structural examination and a restriction of the occipitomastoid suture at the jugular foramen is identified. This somatic dysfunction is most associated with

Ans: Jugular foramen → vagus → OA-C2 → upper GI (stomach) → gastritis

Why: The vagus nerve exits the jugular foramen, so occipitomastoid restriction irritates it. Vagal (OA-C2) reflexes include the upper and middle GI tract, so gastritis fits.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

A, C, and D involve the distal colon, rectum, and bladder, which get parasympathetics from S2-S4, not the vagus. E is wrong because the vagus slows the heart (bradycardia). CN IX, X, XI and the internal jugular vein pass through the jugular foramen.

637asked 3×2026Parasympathetic levels

A newborn receives a structural examination and a restriction of the occipitomastoid suture at the jugular foramen is identified. Treatment is then focused on the occiput and atlas. This may affect which of the following visceral structures?

Ans: Occiput/C1 → vagal reflexes → upper/middle GI incl. pancreas

Why: The occiput, C1, and C2 carry the vagal parasympathetic reflexes for the heart, lungs, upper and middle GI tract, pancreas, liver, gallbladder, kidney, and proximal ureter.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

B (bladder) gets parasympathetics from S2-S4. A (adrenal) is a sympathetic T10 target. D and E are not on the vagal OA-C2 list.

638asked 3×2026Parasympathetic levels

A young female presents with periumbilical discomfort which later migrated to the right lower quadrant. She has an associated fever and is experiencing anorexia and nausea. Which of the following spinal segments may alter the parasympathetic innervation to the diseased organ?

Ans: Appendicitis → midgut → vagus → OA/AA (C1-C2)

Why: This is appendicitis. The appendix is midgut, whose parasympathetics come from the vagus, linked to the OA, C1, and C2 (AA).

Explanation & sources

Explanation

C and D are sympathetic levels (the appendix sympathetic level is T10-T11 right). E (S2-S4) covers the descending colon, rectum, and pelvic organs, not the appendix. C7 has no autonomic role here.

639asked 3×2026SNS vs PNS effects

A young female presents for osteopathic manipulation. During the structural exam a lesion at T3 is identified. Stimulation of the sympathetic chain ganglia at this region may contribute to

Ans: T3 = head, neck, heart, lungs → sympathetic → tachycardia

Why: T3 lies in the head, neck, heart, and lung range. Sympathetic stimulation there speeds the heart (tachycardia).

Explanation & sources

Explanation

A, B, C, and D are all parasympathetic effects. Sympathetic effects at this level would be bronchodilation, mydriasis, reduced glandular secretion, and sweating. Detrusor contraction comes from S2-S4.

640asked 3×2026SNS vs PNS effects

A teenage male presents to urgent care with an acute panic attack. The autonomic nervous system is most likely in sympathetic overdrive. This is associated with which of the following?

Ans: Panic → fight or flight → tachypnea, tachycardia, mydriasis

Why: Fight or flight raises the respiratory rate and heart rate and dilates the pupils and bronchi.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

A is backwards; the sympathetic system drives glycogenolysis to free energy. B is backwards; GI motility falls. D and E are parasympathetic effects.

641asked 3×2026SNS vs PNS effects

A young female presents with periumbilical discomfort which later migrated to the right lower quadrant. She has an associated fever and is experiencing anorexia and nausea. An increase in the sympathetic tone to the abdominal cavity will result in an increase in

Ans: Sympathetic → mobilize fuel, slow gut → gluconeogenesis up

Why: Sympathetic tone makes the liver release fuel through gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Sympathetic tone slows the gut: it decreases motility (A), absorption (B), and secretions (D, E), relaxes the gut wall, and contracts sphincters. Digestive activity is parasympathetic.

642asked 3×2026SNS vs PNS effects

A 45-year-old male presents for a follow-up blood pressure check. Past medical history is pertinent for paroxysmal hypertension secondary to an adrenal pheochromocytoma. Sympathetic stimulation of the involved segment (T10) may cause

Ans: T10 includes gonads → sympathetic = ejaculation ('point and shoot')

Why: T10 supplies the gonads, kidneys, adrenal medulla, middle GI, and lower extremities. Sympathetic stimulation of the reproductive tract causes ejaculation.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Erection is parasympathetic ('point' = parasympathetic, 'shoot' = sympathetic). Sympathetic activation via the adrenal causes tachycardia, not bradycardia. Sympathetic tone decreases lymph flow and pancreatic secretion.

643asked 3×2026SNS vs PNS effects

A newborn receives a structural examination and a restriction of the occipitomastoid suture at the jugular foramen is identified. Osteopathic manipulation is focused on stimulation of the vagus nerve. Treatment will most likely lead to:

Ans: Vagal = parasympathetic → pick the only parasympathetic effect → miosis

Why: Vagal stimulation is parasympathetic. Pupillary constriction is the only parasympathetic effect listed.

Heads up: Textbook key is D. Strictly, the pupil gets its parasympathetic supply from CN III, not the vagus; D wins only because it is the one parasympathetic effect among the choices.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Parasympathetic tone relaxes GI sphincters and increases motility (A and B are sympathetic). It slows the heart and lowers contractility (C is sympathetic). The vagus does not innervate the bladder, and urinary retention is a sympathetic effect.

8.8 · 6 questions · Questions 644–649

Chain ganglia & OMT

No questions in this section match the current Show filter.

644Chain ganglia & OMT

True or false: The sympathetic trunk lies anterior to the thoracic TPs and posterior to the ribs.

Ans: Chain ganglia sit anterior to rib heads → 'posterior to ribs' is false

Why: The thoracic chain ganglia lie directly anterior to the rib heads, near the costotransverse articulation, not behind the ribs.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

This anterior relationship to the rib-vertebra articulation is why rib raising and treating both the rib and the vertebra can influence sympathetic outflow.

Asked in

  • 2025 TA Review Exam 1 (Harlem) · TA review · slides 125-126
Lecture slide (1)
645Chain ganglia & OMT

Sympathetic chain ganglia are located close to the ____ part of the ribs.

AnswerThe head of the ribs (not the neck); the chain ganglia lie just anterior to the rib heads, near the costotransverse articulation.

Ans: Thoracic chain ganglia → directly anterior to rib head → near costotransverse joint

Why: The thoracic paravertebral ganglia lie directly anterior to the corresponding rib head, in close relation to the costotransverse articulation.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

They hang from the segmental spinal nerve by the white and gray rami communicantes, lateral to the T1-T12 vertebral bodies. Upper lumbar chain ganglia lie lateral to the lumbar vertebrae and are reached with deep paraspinal soft tissue work.

Asked in

  • 2023 Exam Review (Montana) Notes - Exam 1 · Instructor review · p.18, Week 8 Autonomics
Lecture slide (1)
646Chain ganglia & OMT

True or false: Somatic dysfunction of the thoracic vertebrae and/or ribs can irritate a thoracic sympathetic nerve.

Ans: Ganglia lie in front of rib-vertebra joint → SD there irritates/inhibits SNS

Why: The sympathetic ganglia sit anterior to the rib-vertebra articulation, so somatic dysfunction of a thoracic vertebra or rib can irritate or inhibit a thoracic sympathetic nerve.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

This is why, to treat the ganglion, you treat both the rib and the thoracic vertebra. Efferent sympathetic nerves synapse in these paravertebral or prevertebral ganglia before reaching their target organ.

647Chain ganglia & OMT

Irritation or inhibition of thoracic efferent sympathetic nerves can occur at which of the following joints?

Ans: Chain ganglia anterior to rib head/costotransverse joint → costotransverse

Why: The thoracic chain ganglia lie anterior to the rib heads and costotransverse articulations, so dysfunction there can irritate or inhibit sympathetic outflow.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Zygapophyseal (facet) joints are posterior, away from the chain. The disc and posterior longitudinal ligament are midline, related to the canal. The thoracolumbar junction is a region, not the joint next to each ganglion.

648asked 5×2026Chain ganglia & OMT

With viscerosomatic reflexes, OMT has the goal of reducing sympathetic outflow. What anatomic area do most of these treatments target?

Ans: Reduce SNS → reach chain ganglia → anterior to costotransverse joint

Why: The sympathetic chain ganglia lie in front of the costotransverse articulation, so treating the rib and thoracic vertebra there (for example with rib raising) targets sympathetic outflow.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Facet joints are posterior to the chain. The psoas is a lumbar muscle, not a sympathetic target. The dorsal horn cannot be reached directly. E is tempting, but the slide names the costotransverse articulation as the area of particular importance.

649Chain ganglia & OMT

What area is of importance when treating viscerosomatic reflexes with OMT?

Ans: VSR treatment → sympathetic chain → costotransverse articulation

Why: The course names the costotransverse articulation as the area of particular importance, because the chain ganglia rest just anterior to it.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Costochondral and costosternal joints are at the front of the chest, far from the chain. Costovertebral (rib head) is the trickiest distractor since the ganglia lie anterior to the rib head, but the course language and rib-raising rationale point to the costotransverse joint.

650asked 5×2026Chapman points

Which of the following best describes Chapman reflex areas or 'points'?

Ans: Chapman point = pea-sized nodule beneath subQ tissue on deep fascia

Why: Chapman points are usually beneath the subcutaneous tissue, on the deep fascia.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

B is half right: they are pea-sized (2-3 mm) but usually tender. C and D are wrong; points occur both anteriorly and posteriorly. E is wrong; anterior points are in the intercostal spaces near the sternum and posterior points are lateral to the spinous processes.

651Chapman points

What best describes a Chapman point?

Ans: Chapman = discrete pea or BB, 2-3 mm, beneath subQ, on deep fascia

Why: A Chapman point is a smooth, firm, discretely palpable 'pea' or 'BB' (2-3 mm) beneath the subcutaneous tissue on the deep fascia.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

A is wrong because Chapman points are usually tender. B describes a Jones counterstrain tender point, which lies in muscle. D is wrong; Chapman points are a form of viscerosomatic reflex and reflect visceral dysfunction.

652asked 2×Chapman points

Which best describes the Chapman's point?

Ans: Chapman point → usually tender, firm, 2-3 mm, on deep fascia

Why: Chapman points are usually tender to the patient.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

A is wrong; they lie beneath the subQ tissue on the deep fascia. B is wrong; they are smooth and firm. D is wrong; they are 2-3 mm. In chronic cases points coalesce and feel bigger. Being tender does not make them Jones tender points, which are in muscle.

653Chapman points

Which of the following describes a Chapman point?

Ans: Slide: Chapman points occur in predictable locations, anterior AND posterior

Why: The slides state that Chapman points tend to occur in predictable locations, usually present both anteriorly and posteriorly.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

A is wrong; they are not in muscle (that is a tender point). B is wrong; they are usually tender. D is wrong; they are on the deep fascia. C is not how the course words it: posterior points are described as lateral to the spinous processes, near the transverse processes.

654asked 2×Chapman points

True or false: Chapman's points are only found on the posterior aspect of the body.

Ans: Chapman points come in anterior AND posterior pairs → false

Why: Chapman points are usually present both anteriorly and posteriorly.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Anterior points are in the intercostal spaces near the sternum; posterior points are lateral to the spinous processes. Colon points are an exception, found along the lateral thigh (IT band). Current thinking is that either the anterior or the posterior point can be treated.

655asked 2×Chapman points

Chapman points: What does one feel like? Where is it located? Is it a tender point? Are they located anterior, posterior, or both? What two systems does it link?

AnswerA pea-like nodule 2-3 mm, smooth and firm; beneath subQ tissue on the deep fascia; not a (Jones) tender point and not in muscle, though usually tender; both anterior and posterior; links the lymphatic and sympathetic nervous systems.

Ans: Pea, 2-3 mm → deep fascia → not a muscle tender point → front + back → lymphatic + SNS

Why: Chapman described the point as a ganglioform contraction that blocks lymphatic drainage; current thinking links the lymphatic system with the sympathetic nervous system. It is a form of viscerosomatic reflex.

Explanation & sources

Explanation

Tender to the patient does not mean it is a Jones tender point, which lies in muscle. Treat with firm, circular pressure for 20-30 seconds; Chapman said to treat innominate dysfunction first.
